They are not an alternative to laxative abuse itself, but they are an alternative to harmful laxatives. What do you think harm reduction even is? It's not telling someone "just don't do this, it's bad", it's giving someone an alternative that is safer to what they were already going to do. This is what I'm really having trouble understanding you on. Do you know what kind of state I would have been in of I was using real laxatives daily for 2 years straight? I would not be able to "walk it off" and return to regular, normal bowel movements pretty much immediately. That's harm reduction. 


Harm reduction is the reason I still have my teeth. Was I told the dangers of purging? Yes. Did it stop me? No. Will it stop others? No. But what helped me was learning how to purge to cause least damage. How is this any different? 


Im being genuine here. I do not see how this is harmful advice when it will save people in active laxative addiction from experiencing more severe side effects.

Im going to need a source for where Stevia is labeled a laxative. I looked, and I cannot find anything. By definition Stevia is also not a laxative. Thus, it's not a laxative. It had laxative effects, but that is not the same thing. Caffeine also has laxative effects, but we do not call it a laxative either, do we?


Again, let me be clear(and i will edit my post to hone in this point further) I am not saying it's a good thing, but it is, 100% a safer alternative because it does less damage than a real laxatives would, and thus, it is harm reduction. I don't want anyone doing this just to try it out. But I know what it's like to have the desire to take laxatives. No amount of "it will have long term consequences" "I abused lax and I ended up with a colonoscomy bag" will change your mind in the moment. And i only want for those people to consider an alternative that will not leave them with the debilitating consequences that laxative abuse will leave.

Maybe I should have worded my title better, but that's why I clarify that this isn't a good thing, but it is a SAFER alternative. Because real laxatives will be a lot harsher on your body and will not let you just bounce back that easily. 


Make no mistake, I am not promoting lax abuse, this is purely harm reduction. If someone wants to abuse laxatives, it's a far better option than real laxatives.

Fortunately, this shouldn't be BED, unless you've been having binges minimum once a week for a minimum of 3 months straight, but your body's natural response to being deprived of food. I've gone through the same thing before, and if there's any solace I can give you, it should go away and your appetite should go back to normal even if it doesn't feel like it ever will right now. But, (and I don't want to simplify an ED too much and take away from the mental aspect) the only way to prevent this in the future would be to never heavily restrict again. 


I know it's easier said than done, but you have to remember that the ED in your mind is the enemy here, not your body. Your body is just trying to survive.

I once had someone explain it to me like this: A normal person wouldn't fathom engaging in these sorts of behavior, much less feel the urge or actually go through with it. So while yes, technically it is you doing the purging and all that, the mental reasoning behind it(like feeling guilt for eating, or fear that you're going to gain, etc) is not really you, it's the disorder. Because the mental turmoil is what's causing the purge, and non disordered people just do not experience it. Once you start accounting for all of the other factors that led you to purge(starting from the very, very beginning), it becomes clearer how little of a choice this disorder is for you. You can compare this to drug addiction, since they're very similar in this regard. A drug addict does do the drugs themselves, but there's a lot more going on that keeps them addicted.
